description: Ubuntu, Alpine, Arch, Debian, and Fedora based Webtop images, Linux in a web browser supporting popular desktop environments.

summary.one_liner: Webtop is a LinuxServer.io Docker image that runs full Linux desktop environments (XFCE, MATE, KDE, i3, LXQt) in a web browser, built on Alpine, Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, or Arch.
summary.what_it_does: Provides prebuilt container images that start a complete Linux desktop session streamed to any modern web browser via the Selkies platform. Many tagged variants combine a base distro (Alpine, Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch) with a desktop (XFCE, MATE, KDE, i3, LXQt), with some flavors supporting Wayland. Ports 3000 (HTTP, meant to sit behind a reverse proxy) and 3001 (HTTPS) serve the web desktop. Configuration uses PUID/PGID for file ownership, TZ for timezone, a /config volume for the user home, and optional GPU passthrough for Intel/AMD and Nvidia drivers. The README also covers HTTP basic auth via CUSTOM_USER and PASSWORD, language selection via LC_ALL, Docker secrets via FILE__ variables, and a umask override. Additional features such as file transfer, clipboard sync, and proot-apps are documented on the external Selkies docs site.
use_cases: run a Linux desktop in a web browser
access a remote Linux desktop from any device
test desktop environments without installing them
run GUI Linux applications in a container
how_to_run: docker run -d --name=webtop -e PUID=1000 -e PGID=1000 -e TZ=Etc/UTC -p 3000:3000 -p 3001:3001 -v /path/to/data:/config --shm-size="1gb" --restart unless-stopped lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:latest
Open https://<host>:3001 in a browser and accept the self-signed certificate
Optional GPU: add --device /dev/dri (Intel/AMD) or --runtime nvidia --gpus all --device /dev/nvidia-modeset (Nvidia)
notable: Multiple distro and desktop combinations selectable by image tag, including Wayland support on several flavors
Minimal-start approach: run a bare command first, then add options one at a time
Automatic GPU detection when a GPU is mounted, with AUTO_GPU=false to disable
Standard LinuxServer.io conventions: PUID/PGID mapping, Docker Mods, and FILE__ secret handling
Documentation for the wider Selkies platform (file transfer, clipboard, gamepads, multi-user orchestration) lives on an external docs site
caveats: No authentication by default; the web terminal has passwordless sudo, so it must be protected before internet exposure
Described as a privileged container with access to the host; not for direct Internet exposure without a reverse proxy
Nvidia GPU support is not available on Alpine images and needs host driver 580 or newer
Requires --shm-size (1gb recommended) and HTTPS for video and audio features
